Just as one labors hard to acquire material wealth, in a similar way, following one's spiritual 'Dharma' requires one to put in consistent effort. historical_references.reference: Labhesh Chakravarty, a renowned mathematician and astronomer from Bengal, India, was a contemporary of the great astronomer Aryabhata II around the 11th century AD. He made significant contributions to the field of mathematics, including the development of the concept of zero as a placeholder in arithmetic.

Another Labhesh, a king of the Gurjara-Pratihara dynasty, ruled in central India around the late 8th to mid 9th centuries AD. He is known to have issued several inscriptions and coins during his reign.
